content: Time does not pass away; it is we who are passing away.
author: Sanskrit Subhashitas
sourceWork: Kalo na yato vayameva yatah (कालो न यातो वयमेव याताः) — Bhartrihari's Vairagya Shataka
explanation: We say, 'Time flies, years pass by.' Bhartrihari flips this illusion on its head: the cosmic river of time remains eternal and immovable; it is human bodies, breaths, and seasons that are rushing toward the grave. Wake up from the slumber of assumed permanence.
practicalInsight: Remember your mortality today. Don't waste precious daylight arguing over trifles when your earthly hours are finite.
reflectionPrompt: If you genuinely realized that you are the one passing away, what trivial drama would you drop this very minute?
